subject: Clarify: net vs gross collection when correspondent bank charges apply
messages:
From: Marco Silva <marco.silva@alpineanalytics.com>
To: ap@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Payment for invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 — intermediary bank fees

Hi Neha / Redwood AP team,

We're ready to send payment for invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 (EUR 42,500) but our bank flagged that the beneficiary account you provided routes through a correspondent bank in the UK and they may deduct intermediary charges en route. Our AP policy requires us to record the full invoice amount on our books — can you confirm whether Redwood expects to receive the gross amount (we should add expected correspondent fees on top) or if Redwood will accept net (we pay the invoice amount and absorb any downstream deductions)?

Also, a quick VAT note: Alpine is VAT-registered in Portugal (VAT PT99999999). Do you need us to apply reverse-charge or provide any additional VAT paperwork?

I've attached our remittance questionnaire and can share the SWIFT trace once the payment is initiated.

Thanks,
Marco Silva
Head of AP — Alpine Analytics
attachments: alf_ap_questionnaire.docx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco.silva@alpineanalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Payment for invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 — intermediary bank fees

Hi Marco — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the questionnaire. Short answer: we prefer to receive the invoice amount gross (i.e., no deductions), and if Alpine's bank will charge intermediary fees, we ask that those are added on top of the invoice so we net the full EUR 42,500.

That said, we can be flexible if you have limitations; if Alpine can only send a single-sum wire with deductions applied by your bank, please let us know and we will document the shortfall and apply a credit policy — but Redwood will need to be made whole in the end.

For VAT: because Redwood is a US entity and this is cross-border service, we generally treat B2B EU customers with VAT reverse-charge when they provide a valid VAT number. Please attach Alpine's VAT registration certificate (or send the VAT number in reply) and we'll mark the invoice accordingly. If you prefer, we can issue a corrected invoice that explicitly references the reverse-charge.

I am copying Laura (finance) and Rafael (payments) to confirm our preferred routing and to provide an alternate EUR collection account that avoids a UK correspondent if available.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: FW: Payment for invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 — intermediary bank fees

Neha / Rafael — forwarding Alpine's question. Quick internal note: invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 was issued net of VAT (US billing) but we can reissue with a VAT reverse-charge note for EU customers when they supply registration. Current beneficiary is EUR account at Redwood's US bank partner (IBAN routed via correspondent bank in London). Treasury preference is to avoid absorbing pass-through charges. If client insists on single-sum payment with deductions, we need a remittance that lists the deducted amounts and we will issue a recovery invoice for the delta.

Alternate options to offer the customer: 1) Provide local EUR collection via our Euro sub-account (no UK correspondent) — will require coordinate with partner bank; 2) Ask Alpine to instruct their bank to add 'OUR' charges on the wire; 3) Accept net payment and bill the shortfall with recovery fee.

I'll prepare two routing options and attach updated wiring instructions (wire_instructions_eur_v2.pdf). Rafael, can you confirm if the Euro sub-account is live and whether it supports SEPA credit transfers from within the EU without correspondent charges?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations
attachments: wire_instructions_eur_v2.pdf
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:30:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Payment for invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 — intermediary bank fees

Laura / Neha — quick confirmation: the Euro sub-account is active but currently held through our partner bank in the EU and supports SEPA inbound transfers without a UK correspondent for accounts inside the SEPA zone. For wires from Portuguese banks, SEPA should route direct and avoid intermediary UK charges. If Alpine's bank is initiating an international SWIFT EUR payment (not SEPA), there is a higher chance intermediary charges will apply.

Two suggested lines for Marco to give to his bank to reduce deductions: 1) use SEPA credit transfer (IBAN + BIC) from a Portuguese bank account; 2) if using SWIFT, instruct OUR charges (payer covers all fees) and include invoice number in Remittance.

I can also issue a short addendum to the invoice noting that Redwood expects gross receipt; that helps our AR team reconcile. I'll draft that and cc you.

— Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts Operations
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco.silva@alpineanalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Payment for invoice RW-INV-2026-1427 — intermediary bank fees

Hi Marco — following up with options so you can pick what works best for Alpine: 

Option A (preferred): SEPA credit transfer from a Portuguese/EU account to our Euro sub-account. This will avoid UK correspondent routing. Use IBAN: [redacted IBAN in wire_instructions_eur_v2.pdf], BIC: [redacted].

Option B: If your bank sends SWIFT EUR, please ask them to set charges to OUR so Alpine covers any intermediary fees on top of the invoice amount. Please confirm in the remittance if they add fees.

Option C (if neither is possible): Send the net amount. If deductions occur, Redwood will issue a recovery invoice for the shortfall plus a small administrative fee. We prefer to avoid this but will work with you.

For VAT: please reply with Alpine's VAT number (PT99999999) or attach the VAT cert. We'll reissue the invoice with reverse-charge wording and zero VAT.

I've attached the updated wiring instructions and reissueable invoice template. Let me know which option you want and we will send the final documents.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: RW-INV-2026-1427.pdf, wire_instructions_eur_v2.pdf
